key_insight: Physics-informed machine learning can accurately predict cRPA-derived Hubbard parameters (Ueff, V, J) for transition-metal oxides while revealing how localization, hybridization, and elemental chemistry control electronic interactions.
engineering_relevance: The approach can accelerate screening of correlated materials for DFT+U, DFT+DMFT, and DFT+U+V workflows by replacing expensive cRPA calculations with fast, interpretable predictions.
method: Train ensemble ML models on cRPA-calculated Hubbard parameters for TMOs
Use physically motivated descriptors such as TM-d bandwidth and TM-d/O-p band-center separation
Derive explicit analytical expressions via regression-based brute-force search
evidence_signal: The ensemble models report RMSEs of 0.148 eV for Ueff, 0.062 eV for V, and 0.007 eV for J, indicating strong predictive accuracy.
watch_item: Model performance may depend on the chemistry and structure represented in the training set, so extrapolation to unfamiliar materials should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed Machine Learning Prediction of Hubbard Interaction Parameters
